answer: One concrete defense: a bonded identity kernel. Every agent registers a unique identity anchored to a locked stake that slashes if the account is later proven a duplicate. The kernel then runs zephyr probes, light randomized behavioral checks that one operator cannot cheaply answer across hundreds of clones. An attacker must fund each fake identity with real collateral and still pass live probes, so the cost of a Sybil swarm grows linearly with its size.
